messages:
Maya: Quick sync — ops + product alignment on the long-term tenant routing roadmap. Need to finalize launch criteria for isolation lanes, canary rollout, and migration expectations. Who's available?

Devon: On it. My current thought: prioritize a "soft-isolation" lane first (rate-limited bursts on shared pools) so we get isolation benefits with minimal infra churn.

Sara: Agree with soft-first. We also need concrete SLOs, eviction policy, and observability hooks before any canary. I'll draft SLO suggestions.

Kevin: From sales perspective: customers are asking for geo-residency + latency guarantees. They'll pay for dedicated capacity, but they want a clear cutover and rollback playbook.

Anna: Customer success here — +1 on migration checklist and rollback runbook. Also need recommended migration windows per region.

Maya: Proposed launch criteria (draft): 1) isolation lane telemetry (p95/p99 baselines), 2) canary with 2 paying customers for 4 weeks, 3) automated fallback to compatible model variants, 4) published docs + migration playbook. Thoughts?

Devon: Add: the model-variant fallback and routing upgrade path must be testable in staging using traffic simulation tools. Also specify capacity reservation for canary.

Sara: Metrics to track during canary: request latency, token cost per request, KV-cache hit rate, tenant eviction rate, and error budget burn. Alert thresholds: p99 latency spike >2x baseline, eviction rate >0.5%.

Maya: Quick config sketch for routing policy prototype (very rough):
```yaml
routing_policy:
  name: tenant-isolation-v1
  entitlements:
    - tier: shared
      routing: best_effort
    - tier: reserved
      routing: quota_isolation
    - tier: dedicated
      routing: physical_isolation
  fallback:
    - prefer: variant_compat
    - degrade_to: smaller_model
  canary:
    enabled: true
    customers: [customer-a, customer-b]
    window_days: 28
```

Devon: We should also define an entitlement matrix (free/shared/reserved/dedicated) that maps to routing flows. That matrix drives billing and infra config.

Kevin: Sales would like pricing bands tied to isolation SLA (bronze/silver/gold) so we can quote cutover SLAs.

Anna: @Devon can you own the migration playbook? @Sara will own SLOs/alerts. I'll collect the customer migration windows and communicate expectations.

Devon: I'll start a playbook draft in the planning doc. Tentative rollout plan: feature-flag -> canary -> 2-week ramp -> general availability. Need capacity estimate for canary.

Sara: I'll post SLO draft by EOD. Also proposing an "eviction sandbox" in staging so we can validate behavior without touching prod tenants.

Maya: Action items: Devon: draft migration playbook (ticket INFR-4121), Sara: SLOs + alert rules, Anna: customer list + migration windows, Kevin: pricing bands. Follow-up sync Friday 10am PT. :calendar: 

deploy-bot: Reminder: infra deploy window Tue 03:00-04:00 UTC — no disruption expected for staged canary.

Kevin: :thumbsup: I'll sync with finance on pricing bands.

Maya: One more question — rollback SLA for dedicated lanes. Proposal: 24h contractual rollback window for Gold customers. Thoughts?

Sara: 24h is aggressive operationally. Recommend 72h for general ops; we can contract 24h for Gold if we pair it with an accelerated runbook and 24/7 on-call coverage.

Anna: Customers typically need ~2 weeks' notice for any migration. We'll communicate timelines if we commit to a 24h rollback SLA.

Maya: Noted. I'll update the launch criteria doc with those constraints and post the updated doc after today's sync. Thanks everyone.
